lateFindings.what: CP1 listed lib/r1BriefCompose.ts as a consumer covered by the change with no per-surface wiring. That is wrong for its FLOOD section, which consumes parcelRecordFactRead.loadParcelRecordFloodFact (the P-152 Consumer-C read) DIRECTLY and UNGATED -- unlike the zoning and setbacks wrappers, whose facts only ever exist for a slated pair.
lateFindings.consequence: Making every non-value flood state a refusal unconditionally (which the first cut of this card did) refuses flood for UNSLATED counties, where the pre-cutover atoms path is still the answer; the ruling forbids that ('unslated rails keep their current path'). Two pre-existing tests in pe-r1-brief-flood.test.ts caught it by failing.
lateFindings.fix: composeFloodBriefSection asks isSlatedForCellServe -- the same one-rule function every wrapper asks -- off the fact's own place_key (the store's <fips>:<prop_id> grammar). Slated: value/absent-verified as before, not-applicable is the stated absence, refused/unaccounted is a declared refusal with the cell's reason and the atom is not consulted. Unslated, or a read that could not place itself (place_key null): unchanged fall-through, because a read that cannot name its county cannot answer the slate question.
lateFindings.cp1Correction: CP1's surfaces list should be read with this amendment: r1BriefCompose.ts's zoning and setbacks sections and smartSiteStub.ts do consume wrapper-gated facts, exactly as CP1 says; its flood section did not, and now asks the slate itself.

lateFindings.what: CP1 published this card's shared fixture to the engine lane as `{ _ruleId, pinnedRowNames, rows }` and called the pinned rows 'the rows a copy may not quietly drop'. The file as first landed (542e771a) carried _ruleId and rows only: the pinned list lived as a hardcoded constant inside cellServeRule.test.ts, so an engine-lane copy would have carried no such list and the file and the test could have diverged silently.
lateFindings.consequence: The exact class of defect a shared fixture exists to prevent, and it was a shape published to another repo -- leaving it as a test-side constant would have made CP1's stated contract false for every reader.
lateFindings.fix: commit 8ba40cc8: the fixture gains pinnedRowNames (the 11 row names) plus the reason the field exists, and cellServeRule.test.ts asserts the FILE's list equals its own PINNED_ROW_NAMES as well as the per-name presence check against rows. missionPremise: P-297 (operator ruling A-193, _decisions/2026-09-16_county_verdict_is_not_the_serve_switch.md, OPS-24 law 7): the (county, rail) gate verdict is a completeness and publish GRADE, not the serve switch. Until this card, resolveAllowlistState returned `record` only on a PASSING county verdict and 19 wrapper modules followed it, so a single `unaccounted` cell on a rail anywhere in a county switched every parcel in that county back to the stale bake; setbacksFactServeCutover.ts is the rail A-192 named. The law: on a slated pair the parcel's OWN cell is the answer -- a value cell serves its value, an absent cell serves the stated absence, a refused/unaccounted/malformed cell (or no row at all) is a DECLARED REFUSAL with its reason, and the legacy or baked value is never the answer. An unslated pair is untouched. P-269 is folded in: cadRollFactFromParcelRecord.ts's four functions must return declared refusals for refused/malformed cells instead of legacy values (its own mission card is marked withdrawn and says so). All of those premises held at source: verified at 9ce30b81 by reading the 19 wrappers and the switch, and verified live against the factory store at 2026-09-16T23:35:47Z for the consequence.
completionPredicate: On a slated (county, rail) pair, the customer-visible answer for a parcel comes from that parcel's own parcel_record_cell irrespective of the county's gate verdict: a value cell serves the value, an absent-verified or not-applicable cell serves the stated absence, and a refused, unaccounted, malformed or missing cell is a declared refusal carrying the cell's reason -- while an unslated pair keeps its pre-cutover path byte-identically, and no production code branches on the county verdict to decide what to serve. Built and measured here at code level (rule, all 19 wrappers, the facets payload, the MCP/stub surfaces, the brief; 158/158 pass pairs byte-identical, 0 changed answers), but NOT observed on a served surface because nothing is deployed; hence closed-partial.
scopeBasis: Dispatch _dispatches/2026-09-16_p297-cell-serve-ldt_dispatch.md (PLAN-ROWS P-297 + P-269, repo legacy-design-tools, FAN-DEPTH 0), under OPS-24's program law (one county at a time; the gate's three names; CODE-DONE != CUSTOMER-DONE) and the canon preamble's ledger-is-the-serving-path ruling. Build scope: artifacts/api-server/ ONLY -- no slate change, no publish gate, no gate scheduler, no factory writer, no deploy, no sub-agents, no writes to any store. Deliberate exclusions, each named: (a) the hauska-engine half is a separate lane and was not touched; (b) buildableEnvelope/ and the P-249 map branch were not touched; (c) no merge was issued (merge authority is the operator's); (d) the rule's form/absenceVerdict/refusalCode fields are asserted by the rule's own test and pinned by the fixture but no production wrapper reads them -- deliberate, since each adapter owns its rail's wire vocabulary, and named in the PR body's reviewer notes so a reviewer does not mistake it for dead code.
controlsThatWouldHaveToFail: For this close to be wrong, one of these would have to be false -- each is measured, not assumed: (1) the 11 check-runs on head 8ba40cc8 concluded success (read from the check-runs API, literal strings above); (2) the five falsifiers really do fire when the ruling is violated (each mutation was performed and reverted, with the failure counts recorded above); (3) the live store really is all-pass on the slated pairs, so the change is byte-identical today (one read-only snapshot, SQL published); (4) the source-level scan really does find the cutover modules it claims to scan and really does fail on a re-imported verdict reader (proven by mutation); (5) no production file imports the old switch (git grep, plus the test).

leave_behind: FOR THE INTEGRATION SEAT -- merge, deploy BOTH halves, then GRADE: PR #710 is OPEN, MERGEABLE, every one of its 11 checks concluded success, and it is BEHIND main only because the base moved. It must land WITH the hauska-engine half (parcel-record-reader.ts's county-scoped `serve` field, a separate lane) before the customer surface changes at all. The graded observation afterwards is one line: a parcel on a slated rail whose cell is `unaccounted` must show a declared refusal carrying that cell's reason on the facets/MCP payload and the brief -- NOT the baked value. If it shows the bake, the old build is still serving; if it shows a refusal with no reason, the cell's own reason is not reaching the wire.

P-256's honest-setback correction is holding on this card: the first `unaccounted` cell on setbackFrontFt in any of the six counties is the real customer-visible trigger for P-297 -- after this lands it becomes a declared refusal for that parcel instead of moving the whole county's rail back onto the bake. Whoever runs P-256 should expect that write to be the moment to grade.

THE RULE'S FORM FIELDS ARE TESTS-ONLY, DELIBERATELY: 17 of the 18 wrappers use loadCellServeDecision purely as the gate (`cell` vs `current-path`) and let the rail's own adapter answer from the same cell, because the adapter owns that rail's wire vocabulary and the rule's refusal codes map 1:1 onto the adapter's. cadRollServeCutover.ts instead asks isSlatedForCellServe per rail because it resolves six overlays from one shared value-basis read. The consequence is that the fixture -- not the function's return value -- is where a reader should look for what the rule PROMISES. Named so it is not mistaken for dead code.

NOTHING ASSERTS A FUTURE ADAPTER MAPS EVERY CELL KIND. The fixture holds the rule honest and the per-rail contract tests hold today's adapters honest, but a NEW rail adapter added later could silently miss a kind the fixture does not know about. A wave-level check over the adapter family (or a fixture that enumerates adapters) would close it. Recorded as debt, not as a control.

THE CONSEQUENCE NUMBER RESTS ON A TRANSCRIBED OLD SWITCH. '0 parcels change today' is only as strong as the transcription of the pre-change rule inside p297CellServeConsequenceCli.ts; the SQL and the counting rule are published in PR #710's body so a reviewer can check the transcription directly rather than trusting the number.

LESSON: AN UNGATED READ REACHING AN UNGATED CONSUMER IS INVISIBLE TO A PER-FILE INVENTORY. CP1 named every wrapper and every caller of the switch and still missed that r1BriefCompose.ts's flood section reads the Consumer-C fact directly. The test pass found it. A CP1 that greps for the READER -- not only for the switch -- would have found it before any code was written.

FALSIFIER TEETH FIND FACTS YOU DID NOT PREDICT: the same mutation that showed the rule's refusal branch is load-bearing for the tests also showed it is NOT load-bearing for the 17 gating wrappers (they gate; the adapter answers). One experiment, two facts, and the second one had to be written down rather than left implied -- it is now reviewerNotes in the PR body.

A CONTRACT PUBLISHED TO ANOTHER REPO MUST BE DELIVERED, NOT DESCRIBED. CP1 told the engine lane the fixture's shape was `{_ruleId, pinnedRowNames, rows}` while the file carried only two of the three; the promise lived in a test constant. If a shape is published across a repo boundary, the check that it holds must live in the FILE that crosses the boundary.

git checkout -- <file> IS THE ONLY SAFE REVERT for a mutation experiment on this machine: PowerShell's (Get-Content -Raw) -replace rewrites every match and can change a file's encoding, so a text-based 'revert' can leave the tree in a state the NEXT experiment measures instead of the committed code.

AN INSTRUMENT THAT CANNOT CLAIM UNMEASURED IS AN INSTRUMENT THAT INVENTS ZEROS: the consequence CLI exits 2 with UNMEASURED when the read-only credential is absent, so the '0 parcels change' answer can never be produced by a missing credential or an empty result set -- and it carries 25 self-test checks so its own predicates can be shown to fire.

Trying to express per-rail coercion inside the shared fixture: 'a value cell whose payload does not coerce into the rail's own domain' is rail-specific (a negative dollar, a zero livingAreaSqft), so the fixture cannot hold it without inventing a rail.
